original-en.context: ROMEO. Well, Juliet, I will lie with thee tonight. Let’s see for means. O mischief thou art swift To enter in the thoughts of desperate men. I do remember an apothecary,— And hereabouts he dwells,—which late I noted In tatter’d weeds, with overwhelming brows, Culling of simples, meagre were his looks, Sharp misery had worn him to the bones; And in his needy shop a tortoise hung, An alligator stuff’d, and other skins Of ill-shaped fishes; and about his shelves A beggarly account of empty boxes, Green earthen pots, bladders, and musty seeds, Remnants of packthread, and old cakes of roses Were thinly scatter’d, to make up a show. Noting this penury, to myself I said, And if a man did need a poison now, Whose sale is present death in Mantua, Here lives a caitiff wretch would sell it him. O, this same thought did but forerun my need, And this same needy man must sell it me. As I remember, this should be the house. Being holiday, the beggar’s shop is shut. What, ho! Apothecary!

modern-en.context: ROMEO. Well, Juliet, I will lie with you tonight. Let me think of how. Oh, trouble, you're quick to enter the thoughts of desperate men! I remember an apothecary who lives around here, whom I noticed recently, in ragged clothes, with heavy brows, picking through medicinal herbs. He looked starved, worn down to the bone by poverty. In his shabby shop, a tortoise shell hung on the wall, a stuffed alligator, and skins of strange fish. On his shelves, a pitiful collection of empty boxes, green clay pots, animal bladders, and musty seeds. Scraps of string and old dried rose petals were thinly scattered around to make the place look stocked. Noticing his poverty, I said to myself, if a man ever needed poison — the sale of which is punishable by death in Mantua — here's a miserable wretch who'd sell it to him. That thought was a premonition of what I'd need, and this desperate man must sell it to me. As I remember, this should be his shop. Being a holiday, the poor man's shop is closed. Hello! Apothecary!
